title: 📰 AI news · November 11
cta: 🔐 Check where my keys are stored

items.title: Railway: attackers hunted for AI keys
items.text: Hosting platform Railway published its final report on the October breach. A hole in its build system led attackers to customer keys, and about $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage followed; up to 100,000 workspaces are at risk. If you run a bot, site or agent on a host, your keys sit in similar settings. Check which AI-service keys you have and replace the ones you no longer need. Free guide "Protecting your computer, code and access": send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: Nitori: up to 37.6M records may be stolen
items.text: Japan's biggest furniture retailer says an attacker was in its system from mid-October and may have taken 37.6 million records: names, addresses, phones, emails, birth dates and orders. Passwords and card data were not affected. Such data fuels phishing, so emails and calls can look convincing. Never share a password, card number or PIN by email or phone, even in the store's name.

items.title: iPhone flaw: a rogue app can read wallets
items.text: Binance warned about a flaw in iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2: a malicious app can read other apps' files, including wallet recovery phrases. A public proof of concept appeared on November 9; no losses confirmed yet. If your phone holds a wallet or a project login, such an app can reach those files. Update iOS and delete apps you don't trust.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon opens to paying developers
items.text: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon after two weeks of testing. Price: $2 per million input tokens and $10 for output. In a hidden-prompt test the model was never fooled, and /swarm turns one prompt into a team of agents.

items.title: Fable 5.2 completes 41% of freelance jobs
items.text: On the Remote Labor Index, built from real Upwork jobs, Fable 5.2 scored 41.3 percent; a year ago the best score was 2.5. Biggest gains came in audio, architecture and 3D models.

items.title: ChatGPT gets business profiles
items.text: OpenAI launched "Businesses in ChatGPT" in beta: companies create a profile, add products and set up agents that answer shoppers right in the chat. For now it covers US online shops and services.

items.title: Ring unveils a home drone
items.text: Drone Cam flies room to room to check where an alarm went off, records in 2K and waits in a dock. It costs $270 and ships January 27.

items.title: Google launches the Pixel Tag tracker
items.text: The $29.99 tag works through Find Hub and a network of over a billion Android devices, runs about a year on a replaceable battery and is IP67 rated.

takeaway: Today keys and data again sit with middlemen: a host, a shop, a phone. When one is breached, everything in its settings is at risk. Recommendation: find where your bot's and agents' keys are stored and replace the ones you no longer need.
